subject: Human Body
title: Antibodies Explained
description: A fast breakdown of Antibodies Explained for builders.

hook.text: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins that latch onto specific invaders like a lock fitting one key.

buildup.text: Each antibody recognizes one antigen — a unique surface marker on a pathogen. The fit must be precise.

discovery.text: Your body can produce billions of different antibody shapes. This diversity covers almost any invader imaginable.

twist.text: Antibodies don't kill directly. They tag, neutralize, and clump invaders for other cells to destroy.

climax.text: Antibodies are precision markers. They find the target and call in the heavy weapons to finish the job.

punchline.text: Antibodies don't kill. They point and say 'get that one.'

quiz.question: What do antibodies do to pathogens?
options: Tag, neutralize, and clump them for other cells to destroy
Heat them until their proteins denature
